budget_items.what_was_said: Chapter 90 is state money for town roads and drainage, paid as reimbursement. A five-year spending plan was prepared at the town manager's request, including equipment.
A reimbursement request was submitted for the first four projects, including mill and paving.
The sidewalk engineering would not all be spent in FY24, with most in FY25.
Chapter 90 is described as not enough for all needed projects.
The plan's balance rises each year because the state adds funding annually, unadjusted for inflation.
A dump truck was hoped for through capital funding, and a mini excavator with trailer is planned in FY26, mostly for stormwater use.
A member asked why the excavator isn't moved earlier given the remaining balance. There is no limit on how much can be used, but it must be paid and then reimbursed.
Draft assumes one big project and two small ones.
Rough first-year estimate includes equipment, with ongoing annual costs lower afterwards.
Projections would apply an annual inflation multiplier.
CI consulting is included in the utility budget with an engineering and audits line.
Earlier estimate per resident was about 60 dollars; with the larger budget it might be around double. Unclear whether it included businesses.

budget_items.topic: Current DPW drainage and stormwater lines
budget_items.what_was_said: Drainage line is nearly spent; stormwater line includes rolled-over funds and is mostly spent.
Stormwater labor in FY23 was estimated, and existing town budget amounts could shift to the utility.
After offsetting existing town budget amounts, net need is lower. Per-household figures were discussed and described as override territory.
Members want Chapter 90 on top of the utility for big projects such as Flat Hill/Page Street.
Nonprofits pay no property tax; the group discussed charging them stormwater fees, with a figure floated.
The labor figure given will be used in outreach budget material.

decisions.decision: Appointment of a vice chair was deferred until all members are present.
Target start for a stormwater utility is FY26; a special town meeting that soon was judged too quick.
Next steps: have CI estimate business footprints/impervious area, then combine with the residential figure, then draft bylaws and specs.
The outreach outline will be emailed to members for comments, with follow-up in about a week.
Next meeting moved to April 18 (third Thursday) because of vacation week.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater utility funding pool and residential fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Consultant described a preliminary annual funding pool and residential fee range comparable to similar towns, and urged aiming higher because of construction cost inflation.
The earlier annual goal was about half the current target; consultant said the same work now costs roughly double.

budget_items.topic: Illustrative spending split of a utility
budget_items.what_was_said: Example split of the annual pool into personnel, equipment payments, replacement of failing catch basins and pipe, and smaller upgrade projects.
Flat fee, equivalent residential unit and impervious-area billing were compared; the middle option was recommended.
Braintree and Chelmsford charge a single residential rate of about the same size per year; Chelmsford has ten tiers.
Members favored adding the fee to the property tax bill to avoid costly separate mailings.
Credits shift the revenue shortfall onto other ratepayers; the group leaned toward deferring credits until the utility is established.
EPA has fined non-compliant communities; consultant gave example fine sizes.
Smaller towns may earmark money for an outside vendor instead of buying equipment used a couple weeks a year.
Discussion of state/federal stormwater funding, asset management grants, 604b, 319 (with cash match) and MVP action grants.
